# Scope

Question: Which original studies (RCTs and NRSIs) compare a larger vs smaller RBC volume per transfusion event (single administration within 6 h) for anemia in hospitalized adults, children and preterm neonates (effectiveness and safety)?
T: 2025-08-05 (explicit in the question). Plugin: biology. Report language: en
Mode: standard. Run name: dossier. No money budget given.

## Criteria
- Population: hospitalized adults, children, preterm neonates with anemia needing RBC transfusion.
- Intervention: larger RBC volume per transfusion (e.g. 20 vs 10 mL/kg; 2 units vs 1 unit; high vs low dose; single-unit policy comparisons).
- Comparator: smaller volume per transfusion.
- Designs: RCT, NRSI (cohort, before-after, case-control). Exclude reviews (list not used except as pointers for study names, only if dated <= T), threshold trials (liberal vs restrictive) unless volume per transfusion is the compared factor.
- Outcomes: Hb increment, number of transfusions, donor exposure, mortality, TACO, length of stay, etc.

## Angles
1. Neonatal/preterm: 15 vs 20 mL/kg, 10 vs 20 mL/kg, small volume, donor exposure, satellite packs.
2. Pediatric: 10 vs 20 mL/kg, severe anemia malaria/Africa (TRACT trial, volume), sickle cell, oncology.
3. Adult: single-unit vs double-unit, one unit at a time policy, dose of RBC, oncology/hematology outpatients/inpatients, ICU, GI bleeding.
4. Dose-response/NRSI: Hb increment per unit, transfusion volume cohort, before-after single-unit policy.
5. Registries: ClinicalTrials.gov trials of RBC volume/dose.
6. Safety: TACO, volume overload, transfusion-associated necrotizing enterocolitis relating to volume/rate.
7. Terms: "transfusion volume", "aliquot", "transfusion dose", "mL/kg", "equal volume", "unit-by-unit".
Reviews <= T may be pointers.

## Budget split
Wave 1: 4 searchers x ~10 calls. Minimum saturation wave: 8 calls.

## Provisional findings
1. Neonatal volume trials. 2. Pediatric volume trials. 3. Adult single vs double unit studies. 4. Observational/NRSI. 5. Safety/ongoing registered trials. 6. Gaps.

## Waves
- Wave 1 (searches 1-4): 48 calls, ~14 eligible studies.
- Wave 2 (search 5 + read of possibles, 6): 13 calls, new eligible: Paul 2002, Berger 2012 (+ borderline Cheema 2022, 2009 Dutch cohort). Gateway cap (60) reached: stop at ceiling, not on saturation.
- Plan revision: findings = neonatal RCTs/cohorts; pediatric TRACT; adult single vs double unit RCTs; adult NRSI before-after; gaps. No change >50%.
